Overview

Klein Curaçao is the day trip Curaçao is known for: a bare white-sand island ten kilometers off the southeast tip, where turtles graze the seagrass. You get about five hours there, enough to swim, snorkel, visit the lighthouse, or do absolutely nothing. The biggest sailing catamarans making this trip leave Jan Thiel at 8:00 and 8:30 AM, with shaded seating, sun decks, and a grill that works toward lunch. A mixed crowd, a relaxed crew, a day that runs itself.

What to Expect

The catamaran leaves Jan Thiel Beach in the morning, crosses to Klein Curaçao, and gives you the middle of the day on and around the island before sailing home by late afternoon.

1
Check-in at the pier · 7:45 AM

Find your boat and settle in on deck.

2
Morning departure and breakfast · 8:00 AM

Sandwiches and coffee as the coast slides by.

3
Anchor off Klein Curaçao · 9:45 AM

Swim, snorkel the seagrass, or ride the dinghy ashore.

4
BBQ lunch on board · 12:30 PM

Grilled meats and salads; alcohol service starts.

5
Afternoon around the island · 1:30 PM

Free time on the beach, in the water, or on deck.

6
Sail home to Jan Thiel · 2:45 PM

Sails up when the wind allows, drinks still flowing.

7
Dock at Jan Thiel · 4:30 PM

Sails down, lines tied, day done.

Meeting & Pickup

Meeting point

Pier at Zanzibar Beach & Restaurant, Kaya Damasco, Jan Thiel Beach, Willemstad. Check in 15 minutes before your departure: 7:45 AM for the 8:00 boat, 8:15 AM for the 8:30 boat.

Open in Google Maps

Hotel pickup (From $19 p.p.)

Optional paid pickup covers hotel zones across the island, as far west as the Kunuku resort. Book it at least 24 hours ahead; you choose your pickup location during checkout.

Important Info

Not suitable for

  • Not wheelchair accessible: boarding and the beach landing involve steps and a swim or dinghy transfer
  • Not suitable if you have a heart condition or another serious medical issue
  • Expecting mothers should check with a doctor first: it's an open-ocean crossing with no medical facilities on the island

Know before you go

  • The crossing can be choppy; take seasickness medicine beforehand if you're sensitive
  • About 1 hour 45 minutes of sailing each way leaves roughly five hours at the island
  • Alcohol service starts around 12:30 PM, after the anchor drops; the bar checks ID for 18 plus
  • Klein Curaçao is uninhabited: no shops and no toilets ashore; the boat's two toilets stay open all day
  • Plenty of beach chairs and palapa shade for the boat's guests
  • A limited set of snorkel masks is free on board, first come, first served; fins are not provided
  • Turtle sightings are common in the seagrass, never guaranteed
  • Vegetarian and gluten-free lunch options are available when requested in advance
  • Weather calls are the operator's; a cancelled sailing moves to a new date or refunds in full
  • Cruise passengers take note: the schedule doesn't fit port calls, so the operator advises against booking

What to bring

  • Reef-safe sunscreen, so the reef stays as healthy as you found it
  • Your own towel; you'll want it after swimming
  • A dry bag keeps your phone safe from spray
  • Your own snorkel fins if you use them
  • Some cash if you'd like to tip the crew
